library(tidyverse)
library(DT)

library(gggenes)

```

# Getting the data for the report
```{r load data}
#Bakta
lines <- readLines(snakemake@input[["bakta_tsv"]])
header_line <- grep("^#Sequence", lines)
bakta_tsv <- read_tsv(
    paste(lines[header_line:length(lines)], collapse = "\n"),
    col_names = TRUE
) %>%
    rename_with(~ str_remove(., "^#"))

bakta_txt <- readLines(snakemake@input[["bakta_txt"]])
get_val <- function(key) {
  line <- grep(paste0("^\\s*", key, ":"), bakta_txt, value = TRUE)
  trimws(sub(".*:\\s*", "", line))
}

genome_length <- paste0(get_val("Length"), " bp")
gc_content <- paste0(get_val("GC"), " %")
coding_density <- paste0(get_val("coding density"), " %")
n_trna        <- get_val("tRNAs") 
n_tmrna        <- get_val("tmRNAs")
n_rrna        <- get_val("rRNAs")
n_ncrna        <- get_val("ncRNAs")
n_cds         <- get_val("CDSs")
n_pseudogenes <- get_val("pseudogenes")
n_hypothetical <- get_val("hypotheticals")
n_sorf <- get_val("sORFs")
n_orics <- get_val("oriCs")
n_orivs <- get_val("oriVs")
n_orits <- get_val("oriTs")
bakta_version <- get_val("Software")
db_version    <- get_val("Database")

#EggNOG
ann_lines <- readLines(snakemake@input[["eggnog_annotations"]])
emapper_version <- grep("^## emapper", ann_lines, value = TRUE) %>%
    str_extract("emapper-[\\d\\.]+-\\w+")
ann_header <- grep("^#query", ann_lines)
eggnog_ann <- read_tsv(
    paste(ann_lines[ann_header:length(ann_lines)], collapse = "\n"),
    comment = "##",
    col_names = TRUE
) %>%
    rename(query = `#query`)

orth_lines <- readLines(snakemake@input[["eggnog_orthologs"]]) 
orth_header <- grep("^#qseqid", orth_lines)
eggnog_orth <- read_tsv(
    paste(orth_lines[orth_header:length(orth_lines)], collapse = "\n"),
    comment = "##",
    col_names = TRUE
) %>%
    rename(query = `#qseqid`)

eggnog_combined <- eggnog_ann %>%
    left_join(
        eggnog_orth %>% select(query, sseqid, pident, qcov, scov),
        by = c("query", "seed_ortholog" = "sseqid")
    )

#ABRicate
abricate_summary <- read_tsv(snakemake@input[["abricate_summary"]], comment = "") %>%
    mutate(`#FILE` = str_extract(`#FILE`, "abricate_(\\w+)\\.tab", group = 1)) %>%
    rename(Database = `#FILE`)

abricate_hits <- map_dfr(
    c(snakemake@input[["abricate_ncbi"]], 
        snakemake@input[["abricate_card"]], 
        snakemake@input[["abricate_resfinder"]]),
    function(f) {
        db_name <- str_extract(basename(f), "abricate_(\\w+)\\.tab", group = 1)
        read_tsv(f) %>% mutate(source_db = db_name)
    }
)

abricate_mincov <- snakemake@params[["abricate_mincov"]]
abricate_minid  <- snakemake@params[["abricate_minid"]]

#Metagraph
metagraph_raw <- fromJSON(snakemake@input[["metagraph"]], simplifyVector = FALSE)

metagraph_top <- map_dfr(metagraph_raw, function(entry) {
    querry <- entry$query_id
    results <- entry$raw_results$results

    if (length(results) == 0) {
        return(
            tibble(
                query = querry,
                sequence_id = NA_character_,
                organism = NA_character_,
                normalized_score = NA_real_,
                database = NA_character_,
                geo_loc_name = NA_character_,
                sequence_url = NA_character_,
                biosample = NA_character_
            )
        )
    }

    scores <- sapply(results, function(r) r$table_data$normalized_score)
    top <- results[[which.max(scores)]]

    tibble(
        query = querry,
        sequence_id = top$table_data$sequence_id,
        organism = top$table_data$organism,
        normalized_score = top$table_data$normalized_score,
        database = top$table_data$database,
        geo_loc_name = top$enrichment$geo_loc_name,
        sequence_url = top$table_data$sequence_url,
        biosample = top$table_data$biosample
    )
})

metagraph_all <- map_dfr(metagraph_raw, function(entry) {
    querry <- entry$query_id
    results <- entry$raw_results$results
    if (length(results) == 0) return(NULL)

    map_dfr(results, function(result) {
        tibble(
            query = querry,
            sequence_id = result$table_data$sequence_id,
            organism = result$table_data$organism,
            normalized_score = result$table_data$normalized_score,
            database = result$table_data$database,
            geo_loc_name = result$enrichment$geo_loc_name,
            sequence_url = result$table_data$sequence_url,
            biosample = result$table_data$biosample
        )
    })
})
```

## Bakta results {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

Bakta was used for bacterial genome annotation, identifying genomic features such as coding sequences (CDSs), tRNAs, rRNAs, and other non-coding RNAs.
Using Bakta version `r bakta_version` with database version `r db_version`.

### Overview
 
The following table summarizes the key features of the annotated genome.

```{r bakta_overview}
tibble(
    Feature = c("Genome length", "GC content", "Coding density", "tRNAs", 
        "tmRNAs", "rRNAs", "ncRNAs", "CDSs", "Pseudogenes", 
        "Hypothetical proteins", "sORFs", "oriCs", "oriVs", "oriTs"),
    Value = c(genome_length, gc_content, coding_density, n_trna, n_tmrna,
        n_rrna, n_ncrna, n_cds, n_pseudogenes, n_hypothetical, n_sorf, 
        n_orics, n_orivs, n_orits)
) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "Bakta genome annotation summary",
        filter   = "none",
        options  = list(pageLength = 20, dom = "t"),
        rownames = FALSE,
        class    = "cell-border stripe hover"
    )
```

### Gene annotation

The following table lists the annotated genes, including their sequence ID, locus tag, type, gene name (if available), and product description.

```{r bakta_genes}
bakta_tsv %>%
    select(`Sequence Id`, `Locus Tag`, Type, Gene, Product) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "Bakta gene annotation",
        filter   = "top",
        extensions = "Buttons",
        options  = list(
            pageLength = 20,
            dom = "Blfrtip",
            buttons = c("copy", "csv","pdf"),
            scrollX = TRUE
        ),
        class    = "display"
    )
```

## EggNOG results

EggNOG-mapper was used for functional annotation of predicted protein sequences from Bakta, assigning orthologous groups and COG functional categories.
Selected columns from eggNOG-mapper output include query identifier, seed ortholog, alignment metrics (percent identity, query and subject coverage), 
COG functional category, and functional description.
Using EggNOG-mapper version `r emapper_version`.

```{r eggnog_tabel}
eggnog_combined %>%
    select(query, seed_ortholog, pident, qcov, scov, COG_category, Description) %>%
    datatable(
        caption = "EggNOG annotations",
        filter   = "top",
        extensions = "Buttons",
        options  = list(
            pageLength = 20,
            dom = "Blfrtip",
            buttons = c("copy", "csv","pdf"),
            scrollX = TRUE
        ),
        class    = "display"
    )
```

## AMR genes

ABRicate was used to screen the assembled genome against multiple antimicrobial resistance gene databases, 
including NCBI AMRFinderPlus, CARD, and Resfinder. Genes were identified based on nucleotide sequence 
similarity with minimum coverage of `r abricate_mincov`% and minimum identity of `r abricate_minid`%. 
The summary table shows the presence of detected resistance genes across all screened databases.

```{r abricate_genes}
abricate_summary %>%
    select(-NUM_FOUND) %>%
    kable(caption = "AMR genes detected by each database (% coverage)") %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
        bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
        full_width = TRUE,
        font_size = 12
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

## Gene Map

Annotated genes from Bakta were visualised as gene arrow maps using the gggenes R package. 
The given sequence was divided into 30 kb windows to improve readability, with each window displayed as a separate panel.
Arrow direction indicates the coding strand.
Coloring highlights genes that are either AMR-related (based on ABRicate hits), COG category V (defense mechanisms), or both.

```{r gene_map_setup}
cog_v_genes <- unique(metagraph_top$query)

amr_gene_names <- abricate_summary %>%
    select(-Database, -NUM_FOUND) %>%
    names()

is_amr_gene <- function(gene, product, amr_names) {
    gene_l <- tolower(gene)
    product_l <- tolower(product)
    any(sapply(tolower(amr_names), function(a) {
        grepl(a, gene_l, fixed = TRUE) | grepl(a, product_l, fixed = TRUE)
    }))
}

window_size <- 30000
windows_per_plot <- 40

gene_data <- bakta_tsv %>%
    mutate(
        forward = Strand == "+",
        is_cog_v = `Locus Tag` %in% cog_v_genes,
        is_amr = map2_lgl(Start, Stop, function(s, e) {
            any(abricate_hits$START < e & abricate_hits$END > s)
        }),
        highlight = case_when(
            is_amr & is_cog_v ~ "AMR + COG V",
            is_amr            ~ "AMR gene",
            is_cog_v          ~ "COG V (Defense)",
            TRUE              ~ "Other"
        ),
        highlight = factor(highlight, 
            levels = c("AMR + COG V", "AMR gene", "COG V (Defense)", "Other")),
        label = case_when(
            is_amr | is_cog_v ~ coalesce(Gene, `Locus Tag`),
            TRUE              ~ coalesce(Gene, `Locus Tag`)
        ),
        midpoint = (Start + Stop) / 2,
        window_num = floor(midpoint / window_size),
        plot_batch = floor(window_num / windows_per_plot) + 1,
        molecule = paste0(
            format(window_num * window_size / 1e6, nsmall = 1), " – ",
            format((window_num + 1) * window_size / 1e6, nsmall = 1), " Mb"
        ),
        molecule = reorder(molecule, window_num)
    )

batches <- sort(unique(gene_data$plot_batch))

highlight_colors <- c(
    "AMR + COG V"     = "#FB8500",
    "AMR gene"        = "#8ECAE6",
    "COG V (Defense)" = "#1c7f97",
    "Other"           = "#cccccc"
)
```
```{r gene_map, results='asis', fig.height=32, fig.width=12}
for (b in batches) {
  batch_data <- gene_data %>% filter(plot_batch == b)
  n_win <- length(unique(batch_data$molecule))
  h <- max(n_win * 0.8, 3)

  p <- ggplot(batch_data, aes(xmin = Start, xmax = Stop, y = molecule,
    fill = highlight, forward = forward)) +
    geom_gene_arrow(arrowhead_height = unit(4, "mm"), arrow_body_height = unit(3, "mm")) +
    geom_gene_label(aes(label = label), align = "left", grow = FALSE, min.size = 0) +
    facet_wrap(~ molecule, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = highlight_colors, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    theme_genes() +
    theme(
        strip.text = element_text(size = 12, margin = margin(1, 0, 1, 0)),
        plot.text = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.1, "lines")
    ) +
    labs(x = "Position (bp)", y = NULL)

  cat(knitr::knit_child(text = c(
    sprintf("```{r gene-map-%d, echo=FALSE, fig.height=%g, fig.width=12}", b, h),
    "print(p)",
    "```"
  ), envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Metagraph results

MetaGraph was used to query COG category V (defense mechanism) gene sequences against a large-scale 
sequence search index to identify the closest matching organisms. For each gene, the top hit was 
selected based on the highest normalized alignment score. Results include the matched organism, 
database source, geographic location of the sample, and sequence accession.

### Overview {.tabset .tabset-fade .tabset-pills}

#### Hits quality

```{r metagraph_quality}
metagraph_top %>%
    filter(!is.na(normalized_score)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = normalized_score)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#219EBC", colour = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 5), 
        labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = "", decimal.mark = "")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    ) +
    labs(x = "Normalized score", y = "Number of genes",
         title = "Distribution of top hit scores")
```

#### Top organisms

```{r metagraph_organisms}
organism_stats <- metagraph_all %>%
    filter(!is.na(organism)) %>%
    group_by(organism) %>%
    summarise(
        n_genes = n_distinct(query),
        n_hits = n(),
        mean_score = mean(normalized_score),
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    slice_max(n_genes, n = 15)

ggplot(organism_stats, aes(x = reorder(organism, n_genes), y = n_genes, fill = mean_score)) +
    geom_col() +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_genes, " genes (", n_hits, " total hits)")), 
        hjust = -0.05, size = 3) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Mean score", option = "plasma", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3)), breaks = scales::pretty_breaks()) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 14, color = "grey40"),
        plot.text = element_text(size = 16),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40")
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of distinct genes matched",
         title = "Most common matched organisms",
         subtitle = "Distinct genes matched and total hit count. Color indicates mean match score")
```
